panels.headline: DOUBLE-WEIGHT ROMAN WEAPONS?
panels.body: A strange claim from ancient military history.
panels.narration: Did Roman recruits really practise with weapons twice as heavy?

panels.headline: TWICE THE WEIGHT
panels.body:
Wicker shields and wooden practice clubs.
Source: Vegetius, Book 1, Chapter 11.
panels.narration: Vegetius, a late Roman writer, described wooden practice clubs and wicker shields, each twice the usual weight.

panels.headline: THE WOODEN POST
panels.body:
Repeated attacks and defence.
Morning and afternoon.
panels.narration: Recruits trained against a wooden post, practising attacks and defence, morning and afternoon.

panels.headline: BUT THERE'S A CATCH
panels.body:
Vegetius describes older traditions.
Not proof of every legion's training.
panels.narration: But he was recording older traditions. His account is not proof that every Roman legion trained this way.
